mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil authority in each resident country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every proposed UBO, general partner, director, and POA holder against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, HM Treasury, and Luxembourg Ministry of Finance lists; enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and any suspicious or unusual transactional patterns; the screening results must be documented in a sign-off memorandum prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the official filing language; names must be in the Latin alphabet and must not be deceptive, confusing, or contrary to public order; a non-Latin or foreign name must be transliterated and, if required by the registrar, accompanied by a French translation; the legal form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale' must be appended to the corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Luxembourg Business Registers rejects a proposed name, the applicant must, within one month from refusal, file a written request for reconsideration with the RCS. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification. As an alternative, the applicant may immediately modify the rejected name and submit a new application for name clearance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office / domiciliation is accepted only where the arrangement is made through an approved professional domiciliation agent in accordance with the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation and related CSSF rules. A virtual office may not substitute for economic substance in tax or VAT terms; the SCSp must maintain a physical service address, local management, and adequate staffing for its email-infrastructure and newsletter-hosting business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% unannounced on-site inspection within the first three years for a low-risk, non-licensed email SaaS SCSp

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (the '1915 Law'), in particular Article 101 and related provisions as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); supplemented by the Luxembourg Law of 14 August 2000 on electronic commerce for information society services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg, operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership agreement (contrat de société) executed in private form or by notarial deed, deposited with the RCS together with the statutory company registration form and ancillary annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital is prescribed by law for the SCSp; the partnership agreement freely defines the capital structure. No statutory escrow account or blocked bank deposit is required; contributions may be made in cash, in kind or in services, and no bank attestation is legally mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER AS MANAGEMENT BODY OF [•] SCSp dated [•]:

WHEREAS the Partnership was formed under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, as amended;

RESOLVED:
1. The executed partnership agreement is adopted in its entirety.
2. All subscriptions to partnership interests are accepted and capital contributions shall be made per Schedule A.
3. The registered office is fixed at [•], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
4. [•] is appointed managing partner (gérant) with sole power to bind the Partnership, open bank accounts and execute agreements.
5. The managing partner is authorized to file the RCS incorporation dossier and complete all tax, VAT, beneficial-owner and regulatory registrations.
6. All prior acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance, drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — online RCS name-search portal (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the proposed SCSp name is available and distinguishable in the RCS database; reject names conflicting with existing or reserved registrations. Draft the partnership agreement containing the statutory minimum content: name, registered office, corporate purpose, term, identity of general and limited partners, capital and distribution rules, management and representation clause. The agreement may be drafted in English, French, German or Luxembourgish and must be signed by all partners; notarization is optional unless real estate is contributed.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all general and limited partners
Proof of residential address of each partner
Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Consent of the owner of the registered office address (lease or hosting agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or identity, propose up to three alternative names in a fresh application; any structural defects in the draft are cured by amending the partnership agreement before signature without additional state fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the incorporation dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers, Luxembourg City (eRegistre portal or LBR counters)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership agreement, the RCS company registration form, the registered office consent and the statutory annexes via the secure eRegistre portal or at the LBR head office. If the general partner is a corporate entity, its certified constitutional documents and an extract from its home registry must be annexed. Pay the EUR 19 registration fee (approx. USD 22) plus any publication fees by card or direct debit. The RCS verifies legal compliance and allocates the business registration number (immatriculation).
required_dossiers: Executed original partnership agreement (private deed or notarial)
RCS company registration form (new entity inscription form)
Certified identity documents and residence proof of partners
Registered office consent/lease
Certified excerpt of the corporate general partner, if any, and its board resolution
Power of attorney for counsel filing on behalf of the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or suspension due to incomplete documents, cure the deficiency within 15 working days by uploading the missing exhibits electronically; if not remedied in time, the file is closed and a new filing with a fresh fee is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium (RESA) and issuance of the RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) — LBR editorial office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful RCS inscription, the LBR automatically transmits the registration to the RESA Official Gazette for publication within three working days. Review the published notice for accuracy, download the official RCS extract and certificate, and retain the extract for banking, tax and licensing use. Legal opposability to third parties is effective on the date of RESA publication.
required_dossiers: RCS registration receipt
Pre-validated publication notice prepared by the RCS
Request for official RCS extract (secrétariat du RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice contains factual errors, file a written correction request with the LBR within 10 days; rectification is processed free of charge and a corrected extract is re-issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT and business-tax registration with the AEDT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Luxembourg City registration office (eCDF online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the RCS registration number, access the eCDF portal and submit the VAT registration application (individual VAT number) for the SCSp in the name of the general partner. Describe the email infrastructure SaaS activity, expected annual turnover and payment rails used. The SCSp, though tax-transparent for income tax, is separately identified for VAT purposes; VAT registration is mandatory for taxable supplies in Luxembourg. Retain the VAT certificate and confirm the effective starting date of taxable activities.
required_dossiers: RCS extract not older than three months
Identity documents of the managing partner (gérant)
Signed VAT registration application (eCDF online form)
Description of the digital services and anticipated turnover
Bank account details of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries the taxable nature or starting date, submit a sworn statement and the first service contracts; late VAT registration is cured by immediate filing, and any back-dated VAT liability may be mitigated by showing the exact commencement date of billing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the beneficial-owner declaration (RBE register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the RBE declaration via the eRegistre portal identifying every ultimate beneficial owner holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of the partnership interests or exercising control through the general partner. Enter for each UBO full name, date and place of birth, nationality and residential address, together with the ownership chain. A separate RBE entry must be made for the general partner entity if it is the registered manager.
required_dossiers: RBE online declaration form
Ownership structure chart covering the full holding chain
Identity documents of each UBO
Declaration of the management powers of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Non-filing within the deadline triggers administrative fines of up to EUR 1,250 and daily penalties of up to EUR 250; file immediately with a covering note explaining the delay and, if assessed, apply for mitigation by demonstrating prompt voluntary cure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board. Information society services under ISIC 6201 (bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting) are exempt from prior authorization under the Luxembourg Law of 14 August 2000 on electronic commerce and Directive 2000/31/EC; the Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) and the CNPD (data protection) supervise the activity without a sectoral license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required; only RCS registration, VAT registration and GDPR/CNPD compliance obligations apply to the email infrastructure SaaS business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is purely immaterial and does not constitute a classified establishment under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments, nor an installation subject to screening under the Law of 19 March 2013 on environmental impact assessment. No EIA report or environmental permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Nothing applicable to the core activity: no wastewater, VOC or waste generation. If the company later places IT hardware on the market, Luxembourg WEEE/RoHS transposition obligations apply; any third-party data centers used by the company must hold their own environmental permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational safety and health compliance under the Law of 17 June 1994 monitored by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); municipal fire-safety conformity certificate for the office premises issued by the local commune following inspection by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); structural and load safety evidence provided by the lessor's building permit file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct/income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes. Digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (cross-border e-filing), eCDF (electronic VAT/declaration filing system), and AEDT's myTAX platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) via the guichet unique des formalités; obtain the RCSL business registration number and 13-digit national identification number (matricule). 2) Register for VAT with the AEDT using Form 640 (inscription à la TVA) submitted through the Guichet unique or directly to the AEDT's VAT registration department. Required supporting documents: certified copy of the articles of association (statuts), RCSL extract, identification of the general partner (associé gérant) and its registered office/authorized signatories, description of the electronic/email infrastructure activity, estimated turnover, and, where the SCSp has no Luxembourg establishment, appointment of a Luxembourg tax representative (représentant responsable) unless the EU reverse-charge/OSS rules apply. 3) The SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes, so no corporate income tax registration is made at entity level; each partner must register with the ACD and is assessed pro rata. 4) Obtain the LU-prefixed VAT identification number (typically issued within 1–2 weeks after complete filing); simultaneously register for the EU VIES database and, if B2C digital supplies to EU consumers are expected, for the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) scheme via the Luxembourg OSS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is statutorily fiscally transparent under Article 182bis LIR: profits are not taxed at the entity level; each partner is taxed directly on their allocable share. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is a deemed taxable person (assujetti unique) in its own right under Article 15 Loi TVA, and must therefore charge, collect, and remit VAT. Territorial scope: Luxembourg-resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income allocable through the SCSp (limited in practice to Luxembourg real estate and certain secured receivables). No tax-exempt zone applies to the SCSp in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box election: the SCSp's pass-through status is mandatory and non-waivable for income tax. Available elections and mechanisms: (1) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 60 Loi TVA — election to consolidate the SCSp with financially integrated Luxembourg entities into a single VAT person; (2) OSS election for B2C cross-border digital/electronic services to EU consumers (Article 59c Loi TVA), avoiding foreign VAT registrations; (3) application for an advance tax ruling (tax agreement) with the ACD confirming partner-level taxation, substance, and profit allocation; (4) hybrid-mismatch alignment under the ATAD Implementation Law of 21 December 2018 — for cross-border arrangements (e.g., where a US LLC or other transparent entity holds partnership interests), the ACD may require a 'payee tax transparency' alignment or 'imported mismatch' adjustment to prevent double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes; an election to treat the SCSp as opaque is not available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi TVA), implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-enterprise exemption under Article 57 Loi TVA (domestic supplies only). This threshold is irrelevant for the SCSp's B2B email-infrastructure supplies: B2B digital services are always subject to reverse charge at the customer's EU Member State and no Luxembourg VAT registration threshold applies. For B2C electronically supplied services (newsletter subscriptions) to consumers in other EU Member States, an EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies; once exceeded, the SCSp must register via OSS and charge destination-country VAT. Supplies of digital/email-hosting services to non-EU consumers fall outside Luxembourg VAT entirely.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority e-invoice pre-clearance, API reporting stamping, or digital stamping for B2B transactions. Mandatory PEPPOL-based e-invoicing applies exclusively to B2G invoices (public procurement) since 1 January 2024. B2B e-invoices are accepted (including PEPPOL BIS 3.0 and EN 16931 formats) provided authenticity of origin and integrity of content are guaranteed via EDI (Article 94 VAT Directive-compliant) or a qualified electronic signature. VAT compliance is effected through periodic VAT returns (Form TVA 200), the European recapitulative statement (Article 265 VAT Directive) listing EU B2B customers, and annual SAF-T reporting for large taxpayers. Luxembourg is preparing for the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reforms, which will introduce mandatory transaction-based digital reporting and standard e-invoicing for intra-EU supplies on a phased timeline, but such obligations are not yet in force. E-invoices must be archived in original format for 6 years.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia: For the SCSp's bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting platform, 'export' equivalency is achieved via EU place-of-supply rules rather than traditional goods export: (1) B2B supplies of digital/API services to customers established outside Luxembourg (including other EU Member States) are zero-rated in Luxembourg by operation of Article 42 Loi TVA — the place of supply is the customer's country and the customer accounts for reverse-charge VAT; the SCSp issues an invoice stating 'reverse charge' (autoliquidation). (2) B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (zero effective rate). (3) Physical goods exports (not applicable to this pure software/infrastructure business) would require Article 44 Loi TVA zero-rating with customs proof. Eligibility substantiation: the SCSp must obtain the customer's valid EU VAT identification number (confirmed via VIES), maintain service contracts, API usage and email-delivery logs, bank remittance records, and, where relevant, IP-address/geo-location evidence demonstrating the customer's true establishment, thereby precluding abuse. Failure to substantiate renders the supplies taxable at 17% in Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / Form 072-EX) — required only if physical hardware/equipment is exported; not applicable to pure digital email-infrastructure services
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or transport carrier manifest — for physical goods; replaced for services by the contract, service-level agreement, and API delivery/usage logs
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank statement evidencing cross-border payment receipt from the foreign customer and FX repatriation
VIES-validation record of the customer's EU VAT ID (for B2B reverse-charge supplies within the EU)

Invoice with mandatory reverse-charge mention and the customer's VAT ID, plus service performance records showing the email/newsletter hosting services were actually rendered to the identified customer
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ACD rigorously audit zero-rating and reverse-charge claims, cross-checking VIES data, contractual documentation, service logs, and bank remittance trails. Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating triggers: (1) retrospective clawback reassessment of the 17% Luxembourg VAT for the full limitation period — 5 years from the end of the year of supply, extended to 10 years (or unlimited in cases of fraud); (2) late-payment interest at 0.6% per month (Article 67 Loi TVA); (3) administrative fines of EUR 25 to EUR 12,500 per infringement (Articles 66–67 Loi TVA), increased to up to 100% of the evaded VAT for willful misconduct; and (4) criminal sanctions under Articles 170–175 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law (AO) — imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and fines of EUR 250 to EUR 50,000 (or up to EUR 250,000 for aggravated tax fraud), with the general partner of the SCSp being jointly and severally liable. Repeated non-substantiation can additionally result in loss of VAT registration status, denial of input VAT recovery, and publication of the assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB). Foreign exchange control and capital movement oversight are shared among the BCL, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance, and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT supervision. The applicable legal framework is Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) governing free movement of capital, EU Regulation 2018/1672 on cash controls, the Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. The euro is freely floating and Luxembourg maintains no exchange controls. Both current-account items (subscription revenues, trade payments, SaaS fees) and capital-account items (SCSp capital contributions, partnership distributions, intercompany loan repayments) are unrestricted between Luxembourg and all EEA member states and most third countries, subject only to EU/UN financial sanctions compliance. No prior central bank authorisation, no convertibility licence, no profit remittance approval, and no inward/outward investment screening applies to a non-regulated SCSp of this commercial nature. Non-resident general and limited partners may receive profit distributions via SEPA or SWIFT without BCL or CSSF scrutiny; the only burdens are bank-side KYC, CRS/FATCA reporting, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations filed by the bank for eligible cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no surrender obligation, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no minimum conversion or disposal ratio for export proceeds or cross-border service receipts. The SCSp is free to hold EUR subscription revenue, convert it, redeploy it, or distribute it in accordance with the limited partnership agreement. Resident credit institutions are required to report to the BCL, on a monthly basis, individual cross-border payments of at least EUR 12,500 for balance-of-payments purposes, but this obligation is imposed on the bank, not on the SCSp, and implies no restriction on the SCSp's use of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority_summary_note: For the specific email newsletter infrastructure activity, no licence is required, no securities law registration applies (non-AIFM SCSp), and no banking or payment service licence is triggered because the SCSp is a payee/merchant, not a payment service provider. The sole regulated counterparty for payment acceptance is the PSP (Stripe entity) and for treasury is the Luxembourg commercial bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.banking_aml_risk_classification: The entity is rated Low_Risk_Standard under typical Luxembourg bank risk taxonomies given the ISIC 6201 software-as-a-service activity, transparent ownership structure, and absence of cash-intensive or high-volume payment flows. Enhanced due diligence is nevertheless applied to the SCSp form itself because it is an unregulated partnership with no legal personality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.securitisation_and_fund_regulatory_note: The SCSp is not a securitisation undertaking (Law of 22 March 2004) and is not a regulated fund (SIF/SICAR). Therefore no CSSF approval, no minimum capital, and no annual CSSF reporting apply. A bank may nonetheless request a statutory declaration confirming that the SCSp is not subject to the AIFM Law of 12 July 2013 and does not hold assets for more than one investment policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.rbe_register_deadline: The beneficial owners of the SCSp must be registered in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within one month of incorporation; an updated RBE excerpt is a mandatory component of the banking file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_regime_specific_iso_codes: Reporting currency: EUR. Functional currency of the SCSp may be elected as EUR for statutory accounting; Stripe settlements in USD, GBP, and other currencies are translated at the ECB reference rate. No Luxembourg GAAP restriction prevents multicurrency accounting, but the tax administration and RCS filings suggest EUR as the standard.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.profit_remittance_hurdle_assessment: No statutory or regulatory hurdle exists for profit distribution by the SCSp to non-resident partners. Luxembourg does not levy withholding tax on distributions from a fiscally transparent partnership; the SCSp itself is not subject to CIT or net wealth tax, and partners are taxed only in their respective jurisdictions of residence. The practical hurdle is solely banking: the paying bank will verify the partnership agreement, the RBE, and the distribution resolution before releasing funds to non-resident beneficiaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.financial_sanctions_screening_layer: The bank applies CSSF/BCL circularised EU restrictive measures, UNSC sanctions, and US OFAC lists. The email infrastructure business must provide evidence of geo-blocking and sanctions screening on its subscriber base to avoid frozen funds and reputational blockages.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.balance_of_payments_code_mapping: Inbound equity injections should reference BOP code 521 (shares and other equity in a non-listed partnership) and intercompany loans code 522/523; outbound service payments should reference BOP code 219/2270 (computer and information services), and royalty/licensing outflows code 2310.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.compliance_note_onsubstance: Although the SCSp has no Luxembourg substance requirement (non-AIFM and non-managed commercial partnership), the bank's KYC will assess the central administration seat in Luxembourg, the local registered office address, the local bank account, and the economic rationale for the partnership. The 2018 OECD Substance requirements applicable to CIT taxpayers do not apply to the SCSp because it is tax transparent, but a written substance memorandum mitigates bank refusal.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.esg_and_reputation_screen: Banks may additionally screen the newsletter platform's content for adult, gambling, crypto, and misinformation risks; a content policy and abuse-prevention statement should be included in the KYC file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.anti_money_laundering_law_identifier: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 5 December 2017, implementing the 4th and 5th EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives, and CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.fx_control_summary_conclusion: Luxembourg offers a fully liberalised, euro-denominated treasury environment with no exchange controls, no reporting duties on the entity, and no statutory barrier to cross-border equity injection, income repatriation, or trade disbursement, subject only to standard bank KYC and EU sanctions adherence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Financial viability rating: Medium for operational use, Low for treasury concentration. Luxembourg fully permits the SCSp to hold funds with CSSF-licensed E-Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs), including entities passported into Luxembourg under the Law of 1 August 2018 (PSD2 implementation). Thus, Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Ireland, passported to Luxembourg), Revolut Ltd (Ireland), Wise Europe SA (Belgium), and Mangopay/Market Pay can be used as settlement and fee-collection rails. Legal constraints: (i) funds held at an EMI are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee fund (Fonds de garantie des dépôts Luxembourg, EUR 100,000 protection applies only to credit institutions), (ii) EMIs are subject only to safeguarding obligations, not prudential deposit protection, (iii) post-Brexit, UK-headquartered EMIs can serve Luxembourg clients only via EEA-licensed subsidiaries, and (iv) concentration of treasury balances in an unregulated non-EEA EMI would weaken BCL regulatory oversight and may be treated by the Luxembourg tax authorities and the CSSF-supervised bank as a substance deficiency. Practical recommendation: use Stripe as the payment-acceptance overlay and a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank as the sole treasury account holder; an EMI may be used for sub-account segmentation but must not hold more than 10% of operational treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law permits non-face-to-face onboarding with enhanced due diligence under Article 4 of CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the 5th AML Directive, but the actual market practice of domestic Tier-1 banks is to require an in-person KYC interview at the Luxembourg office for at least one authorised signatory or the General Partner’s director. Remote opening is practically feasible only when (i) the General Partner is a fully regulated EU entity (AIFM, investment firm, or bank) or (ii) the bank accepts e-identification with video verification and digital certification, subject to internal anti-fraud scoring. For the present SCSp with non-regulated partners, the recommended path is: one partner representative attends a physical meeting in Luxembourg; all other signers complete remote identity verification via the bank’s digital channel with notarised powers of attorney certified by a Luxembourg notary or EEA consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is a contractual partnership without legal personality; the notary deed and partnership agreement may not clearly identify all partners, or the bank is required to verify every partner with rights over SCSp assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the SCSp limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) and any private partnership agreement (PPCA); RCS excerpt (trade register) evidencing the entity and the registered office; RBE disclosure receipt; GP corporate file with articles, certificate of good standing, register of directors; partner schedule with country of residence, ownership percentages, and economic rights; notarised or apostilled powers of attorney for all non-resident signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) or partners resident in high-friction jurisdictions (e.g., US, Middle East, Asia) with no prior Luxembourg banking relationship and unclear source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passports and recent utility bills of each UBO; source of wealth declaration on the bank’s standard form; reference letters from the UBO’s domestic financial institution of at least 2 years standing; CVs and executive biographies of the founders; notarised board resolution of the GP authorising the Luxembourg account; bank statements showing the originating accounts for capital injections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital is injected from third-party payment processors (e.g., Stripe settlement runs or crowdfunding sources) rather than directly from partner bank accounts, creating a commingling and source-of-funds transparency concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe commercial agreement and merchant account details; payment routing diagram showing subscriber payments flowing from Stripe’s settlement bank to the SCSp’s Luxembourg IBAN; capital calls and historical bank statements for each partner contribution; financial model showing predictable revenue; evidence of purchase of email infrastructure (AWS or equivalent) matching the business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank flags the authenticity of the SaaS subscription business because the ISIC 6201 activity is digital, cross-border, and not subject to a Luxembourg licence, increasing money-laundering typology concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan for the bulk transactional email API platform; product documentation and customer contracts with two or more seed clients; transaction-level reporting showing average ticket value and monthly API volume; GDPR and ePrivacy compliance policy; sanctions and OFAC screening mechanisms embedded in the platform; data-protection officer letter confirming no prohibited content categories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp has no employees and no visible operational substance in Luxembourg, prompting bank refusal under the 'economic substance' and 'office address' KYC criteria.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office agreement with a Luxembourg corporate service provider; director/GP being a Luxembourg-resident service company or the ultimate commercial parent; proof of Luxembourg bank account as the central treasury account; an annual substance memorandum including local board/admin meeting records; lodged accounts (file with RCS) or a letter from the Luxembourg auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) confirming administrative substance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.bank_selection_rationale: For a cross-border SCSp SaaS treasury in Luxembourg, BGL BNP Paribas and BIL are the preferred Tier-1 anchors due to their deep experience with SCSp vehicles, robust international payment corridors, and compatible KYC tolerance for non-regulated partnerships. Société Générale Luxembourg is acceptable when the partners maintain an existing relationship. Quintet Private Bank is viable only for high-net-worth partners seeking integrated private banking. The onboarding timeline is estimated at 3 to 6 weeks on average, longer if a partner is from a sanctioned-adjacent jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.mobile_banking_and_access_note: All Tier-1 banks provide multi-currency accounts, SEPA/SWIFT channels, direct EUR/USD treasury services, and API connectivity or EBICS access for the IT infrastructure company; the SCSp must ensure a dedicated payment integration via Stripe for incoming card flows, since Tier-1 banks do not efficiently accept card sub-merchant transactions directly.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.alternate_luxembourg_branch_credit_insti: Additional credit institutions available are DZ Privatbank S.A., Raiffeisen Banque, Banco Santander Luxembourg, and BPifrance Luxembourg; however, none offers distinct advantages over the Tier-1 candidates for a pure SaaS treasury, and several require domestic presence of the holding company.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.banking_fees_and_non_interest_terms: Setup fee ranges from EUR 500 to EUR 1,500; account maintenance from EUR 60 to EUR 120 per month; SWIFT outgoing fees from EUR 15 to EUR 25 per message; card acquiring via Stripe carries an interchange plus contract. The SCSp should negotiate multi-currency ledger capability and zero sweep to a money market overnight euro deposit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.liquidity_management_covenant: The SCSp shall maintain a weighted-average liquidity buffer equivalent to at least 3 months of operating expenses in a BCL-supervised credit institution to satisfy bank credit and treasury policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.bank_account_delegation_structure: The General Partner (or a delegated Luxembourg management company) shall hold sole or joint signature authority; at least one EU resident signatory is recommended to reduce KYC friction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: partner equity contributions are remitted to the SCSp's IBAN at the chosen Luxembourg bank via SWIFT MT103 (for non-EUR) or SEPA Credit Transfer (for EUR). In field 50K of MT103, the ordering customer must be the partner’s own account; field 59 must be the SCSp’s account with full legal name; field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'Capital Contribution SCSp' and reference the specific capital call; the BOP purpose code should be 521 (investment in partnership equity) to ensure correct BCL statistical classification. For a convertible loan or shareholder advance, use BOP code 522 (loan to a non-financial partnership). The receiving bank will apply standard verification against the partnership agreement and may require a letter from the GP confirming the capital call. Non-EUR inbound funds are automatically converted to EUR unless a multi-currency account is opened. The SCSp must substantiate each injection in its annual accounts and CRS/FATCA filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SEPA Credit Transfer for EU/EEA vendor and supplier payments (email infrastructure providers such as AWS, SendGrid, Mailgun, cloud computing) with T+0 or T+1 settlement; SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA suppliers (e.g., US data-centre providers) with purpose code 219/2270 (computer and information services). For larger procurement and dedicated hardware/bandwidth contracts, a commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) may be issued but is typically unnecessary and costly. Statutory-safe outbound disbursement protocol requires: (i) valid invoice matching the approved vendor register; (ii) contractual underlying agreement; (iii) sanctions screening of the beneficiary; and (iv) a record of the BOP statistical code. The SCSp may also make distribution payments to non-resident partners via SEPA/SWIFT under the partnership agreement, without any forward contract or hedge, provided that the standard anti-money-laundering transaction monitoring does not flag the beneficiary as an unverified PEP. Payment to Stripe for fees is handled as a recurring merchant settlement charge.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable forward FX contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) with maturity up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA FX Annex or Luxembourg master agreement
FX swaps (swap de change) for temporary liquidity rebalancing between EUR and USD treasury positions

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted-market currencies where settlement is impossible in the local currency (only when a documented USD or local-currency exposure arises from subscribers in such jurisdictions)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to convert a potential intercompany USD loan into EUR, or to align an eventual debt financing with the EUR revenue base

FX zero-cost collar and participating forward structures for budget certainty on high-value annual subscription contracts (speculative naked positions are prohibited by Luxembourg market best practice and bank credit policy)
Overnight FX rolling (TOM/NEXT) for daily liquidity and settlement of Stripe multicurrency balances
FX limit account (compartment) for treasury management without any speculative intent, subject to the board-approved hedging policy, EMIR reporting obligations, and Luxembourg AIFM exclusions
Market-implied forward-rate protection via forward rate agreements is not applicable to an equity-funded SCSp unless it enters into non-programmatic debt instruments
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.clearing_and_settlement_days: SEPA: T0 to T+1; SWIFT MT103: T+1 with value dating; card acquiring via Stripe: T+2 settlement cycle; the SCSp should maintain an intraday liquidity facility at the bank for timing gaps, though this is expected to be minimal for a subscription-based recurring revenue model.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.fx_hedging_policy_note: Luxembourg does not require authorisation for FX hedging by a non-financial counterparty. Under EMIR (Regulation (EU) No 648/2012), the SCSp is a Non-Financial Counterparty (NFC). If it engages only in hedging transactions and its aggregate average notional in OTC derivatives remains below the EUR 3 billion clearing threshold, it qualifies as an NFC- and is exempt from central clearing and margin exchange; the bank counterparty performs EMIR trade reporting to a trade repository, and the SCSp must execute an ISDA Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex or maintain a non-margined FX trading line with its Tier-1 bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.disbursement_control_and_fraud_preventio: A dual-signature authorization regime (one partner plus the finance officer) must govern all outbound payments above EUR 5,000; positive-pay reconciliation against Stripe deposits; daily cash position monitoring via the bank's API; segregated sub-ledger for deferred revenue to satisfy Luxembourg accounting rules on SaaS subscription recognition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_buffer_optimisation: The SCSp shall operate a three-tier liquidity structure: (i) transactional balance at the Tier-1 bank (EUR 50k-100k), (ii) short-term euro money market instrument via the bank, and (iii) a USD/EUR FX line with a notional cap of 30% of annual revenues to accommodate hardware and bandwidth renewal payments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.cross_border_cash_pooling_constraint: If the SCSp is consolidated with a foreign parent, Luxembourg law and CSSF 12-02 do not prohibit notional or zero-balance cash pooling; however, the bank will require a pooling agreement and a positive-interest adjustment to avoid unlawful financial assistance. For an SCSp without bank debt, the safest structure is a EUR concentration account with notional sub-accounts for the non-resident partners, without physical cross-border sweeping.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.regulatory_reporting: The bank files BCL monthly balance-of-payments reports for any cross-border transaction equal to or above EUR 12,500. The SCSp itself has no BCL reporting obligation, but may be asked to provide a 'purpose of transaction' declaration on corporate actions to the bank in advance to facilitate compliance with the Eurosystem balance of payments statistics framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.operational_conclusion: Stage 4 treasury blueprint is fully executable for the Luxembourg SCSp with (i) a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank account, (ii) a Stripe Billing overlay for card merchant income, and (iii) standard OTC FX forward and swap instruments for periodic USD/EUR expenditure mismatches. The jurisdiction imposes no FX permit, no surrender rules, and no profit remittance approval; the entire structure remains compliant with CSSF AML rules, EU capital-movement freedom, and BCL statistical reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.emergency_liquidity_rail: In the event of a bank account freeze or sanctions blocking, the SCSp may initially route operational settlement through an approved EU-EMI (Stripe Payments Europe Ltd or Mangopay) and simultaneously notify the CSSF and the Ministry of Justice; a negotiated 30-day period is standard before any court-ordered asset restriction, though the SCSp should maintain a pre-approved second account at BIL as a redundancy measure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Register Data (Déclaration Confirmative Annuelle) under the Law of 19 December 2020 on commercial and beneficial ownership registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two (2) months following the anniversary of the entity's RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice issued by the RCS; unanswered notice leads to the entity being marked non-compliant, followed by administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) and court-ordered dissolution at the Public Prosecutor's request; statutory fines of up to EUR 4,000 apply to persistent defaulters.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Owner File (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs - RBE), including updates for any transfer of SCSp partnership interests during the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, through the combined RCS/RBE declaration filed within two (2) months of the registration anniversary; in-year transfers of partnership interests must be declared within one (1) month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per UBO for late or missing declarations; public listing of non-compliant entities; restriction on profit distributions; criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 for deliberately false declarations; ultimate risk of de-registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels), management report and, where applicable, statutory auditor's report - required where at least one general partner is a corporate entity; exempt when all general partners are natural persons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by partners within six (6) months of the financial year-end and deposit within one (1) month of approval; effective latest deposit date is seven (7) months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-deposit fines of EUR 250 to EUR 5,000 imposed on the general partner and managers; RCS public default annotation; persistent non-filing triggers formal notice, administrative strike-off and civil liability of the general partner.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
